steps.title: You ask
steps.note: Your message joins the orchestrator's input queue, read by one session at a time.

steps.title: The orchestrator proposes
steps.note: Two guards run before anything is written: quota read less than 30 minutes ago, and no identical wave in the last 24 hours.

steps.title: A mandate is written
steps.note: Objective, scope, access, budget and stop rule, stored as a proposal. Nothing runs yet: the orchestrator cannot start a team itself.

steps.title: You approve, the first time
steps.note: A new thread has no autonomy window, so its first mandate waits for your click. Once you open one, the next mandates start without you.

steps.title: The mission is registered
steps.note: Written as planned before the worker starts, so a PC that never answers still leaves a trace to reconcile.

steps.title: A worker is spawned
steps.note: On the PC: one process, one SDK session, one git worktree. That worker is the team.

steps.title: The lead works
steps.note: It delegates sub-agents inside its own session. Your mid-flight messages are course corrections, never orders to stop.

steps.title: Closing, then lessons
steps.note: Retry, definitive failure or escalation. Lessons are extracted from the transcript and pushed into the next mandate.
